title: Egypt Compared to the Fallen Cedar of Assyria

questions.question: In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the Lord asks Pharaoh, "Whom are you like in your...?"
options: Greatness
Wealth
Pride
Armor
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:2 (ESV): "Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: 'Whom are you like in your greatness?'"

questions.question: To what nation does God compare Egypt in order to warn Pharaoh of his impending fall?
options: Assyria
Babylon
Edom
Philistia
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:3 (ESV): "Behold, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches and forest shade, and of towering height, its top among the clouds."

questions.question: Assyria is compared to a great cedar in Lebanon. How tall did it grow?
options: Its top was among the clouds
Higher than the pyramids
To the throne of God
Above the walls of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Its top was among the clouds
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:3 (ESV): "...and of towering height, its top among the clouds."

questions.question: What made the great cedar (Assyria) grow so great?
options: The waters nourished it; the deep made it grow tall, making its rivers flow around the place of its planting
The fertile soil of the Nile delta
The golden fertilizer of the kings
The continuous rains from the east
questions.correctAnswer: The waters nourished it; the deep made it grow tall, making its rivers flow around the place of its planting
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:4 (ESV): "The waters nourished it; the deep made it grow tall, making its rivers flow around the place of its planting, sending forth its streams to all the trees of the field."

questions.question: Because the cedar towered high above all the trees of the field, what happened in its boughs?
options: All the birds of the heavens made their nests in its boughs
The eagles of Babylon devoured its fruit
The locusts swarmed and ate its leaves
Angels rested in its shade
questions.correctAnswer: All the birds of the heavens made their nests in its boughs
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 (ESV): "All the birds of the heavens made their nests in its boughs; under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth to their young..."

questions.question: Who lived under the cedar's shadow?
options: All great nations
Only the kings of the north
The poor and destitute
The priests of Baal
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 (ESV): "under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth to their young, and under its shadow lived all great nations."

questions.question: No cedar in the garden of God could rival it. What was the reaction of all the trees of Eden (the other nations)?
options: They envied it, that it was in the garden of God
They plotted to chop it down
They withered in its shadow
They bowed down to it in worship
questions.correctAnswer: They envied it, that it was in the garden of God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:8-9 (ESV): "No cedar in the garden of God could rival it... I made it beautiful in the mass of its branches, and all the trees of Eden envied it, that were in the garden of God."

questions.question: Why did God give this great cedar over to the mighty one of the nations (Babylon) to be cut down?
options: Because it towered high and set its top among the clouds, and its heart was proud of its height
Because it produced no fruit
Because it shaded the temple of God
Because its roots drank from a poisoned river
questions.correctAnswer: Because it towered high and set its top among the clouds, and its heart was proud of its height
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:10-11 (ESV): "Because it towered high and set its top among the clouds, and its heart was proud of its height, I will give it into the hand of a mighty one of the nations. He shall surely deal with it as its wickedness deserves."

questions.question: Who cut down the great cedar and left it?
options: Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations
The lumberjacks of Lebanon
The fierce winds of the east
The fiery angels of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:12 (ESV): "Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, have cut it down and left it."

questions.question: What covers the fallen trunk of the cedar?
options: On its fallen trunk dwell all the birds of the heavens, and on its branches are all the beasts of the field
Snow and ice from the mountains
Weeds and thorns of the wilderness
The ashes of its burned leaves
questions.correctAnswer: On its fallen trunk dwell all the birds of the heavens, and on its branches are all the beasts of the field
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:13 (ESV): "On its fallen trunk dwell all the birds of the heavens, and on its branches are all the beasts of the field."

questions.question: What is the lesson given so that none of the trees by the waters may grow to towering height?
options: For they are all given over to death, to the world below, among the children of man, with those who go down to the pit
That they should share their water with the smaller trees
That they must produce more fruit
That God prefers the lowly bushes
questions.correctAnswer: For they are all given over to death, to the world below, among the children of man, with those who go down to the pit
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:14 (ESV): "All this is in order that no trees by the waters may grow to towering height... For they are all given over to death, to the world below, among the children of man, with those who go down to the pit."

questions.question: What did God make the deep do on the day the cedar went down to Sheol?
options: He made the deep mourn for it and restrained its rivers, and many waters were stopped
He made the deep boil like a pot
He turned the deep to blood
He filled the deep with Leviathans
questions.correctAnswer: He made the deep mourn for it and restrained its rivers, and many waters were stopped
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:15 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord God: On the day the cedar went down to Sheol I caused mourning; I closed the deep over it, and restrained its rivers, and many waters were stopped."

questions.question: What happened to the nations at the sound of the cedar's fall?
options: God made the nations quake at the sound of its fall
The nations rejoiced and sang a new song
The nations gathered its wood for their own palaces
The nations sought an alliance with Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: God made the nations quake at the sound of its fall
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:16 (ESV): "I made the nations quake at the sound of its fall, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit."

questions.question: Who were comforted in the world below (Sheol) when the great cedar fell?
options: All the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water
The kings of Judah and Israel
The giants of old, the Nephilim
The spirits in prison
questions.correctAnswer: All the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:16 (ESV): "and all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the world below."

questions.question: Because Pharaoh is like the cedar in greatness, what is the final verdict for him and his multitude?
options: "You shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below... This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord God."
"You shall escape to the rivers of Cush."
"You shall reign in Sheol forever."
"Your roots will sprout a branch from Babylon."
questions.correctAnswer: "You shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below... This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord God."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:18 (ESV): "Whom are you thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? You shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below... This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord God."

key_verse_text: "Whom are you thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? You shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below. You shall lie among the uncircumcised, with those who are slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord God."
